findings.observed: The files declare kelvin, but h5netcdf returns the one-character unit as bytes (b'K') and the unit check compares its text form with 'K'. The call raises: 'tasmax' is published in "b'K'", but recipe 'txx' converts from 'K'. Precipitation is unaffected.
findings.title: Temperature recipes (txx, tnn) fail on real NEX files

findings.consequence: A gridded curve can rest on far fewer years than the request suggests where data are missing; the number of years behind each cell's fit should be checked before use.
findings.documented: docs/sources/jrc.md:58: 'The curated policy fits the lower tail and requires at least 20 complete years.' The policy's own error message says it 'requires at least 20 complete years' (crc_sdk/workflows/blocks.py:126-129).
findings.observed: validate_years compares the number of years in the request with minimum_years (crc_sdk/workflows/blocks.py:124-125). Each grid cell is then fitted when it has at least 4 valid annual values (MINIMUM_BLOCKS = 4, crc_sdk/connectors/blocks.py:60; minimum_blocks=4 in crc_sdk/providers/era5.py:566 and crc_sdk/providers/cmip6.py:1052). Station sources apply minimum_years per station.
findings.title: The 20-year minimum counts the years requested, not the years valid in each cell

findings.consequence: A JRC flood or EDO file, once moved away from its cache, does not say under which licence or from which bytes it was made.
findings.documented: docs/data-licences.md:14-15: 'Every canonical file records source.licence, source.attribution, retrieved_at and checksum (schema 1.3), so outputs self-describe.'
findings.observed: Those fields are written only when the curve source supplies a CurveSourceInfo (crc_sdk/connectors/adapters.py:309). The JRC and EDO modules define none; the JRC workflow only rewrites the uri (crc_sdk/workflows/jrc.py:521-534). Checksums of the cropped inputs are kept in the cache manifest, not in the output file. Applies to jrc-edo as well.
findings.title: JRC flood and EDO output files do not carry licence, attribution, retrieval time or checksum

findings.consequence: An EDO file and an ERA5 or CMIP6 file built over the same years would carry different horizons and would not join on the row key.
findings.documented: docs/design-decisions.md:28-30: for a window, 'horizon = centre year (start + end) // 2'. docs/sources/cmip6.md:42: 'horizon is the window centre'.
findings.observed: The EDO provider sets the year of its record to max(years) (crc_sdk/providers/jrc_edo.py:217).
findings.title: EDO drought curves are labelled with the last year of the record, not the centre year

findings.consequence: A year with most of its record missing still contributes an annual minimum to the fit.
findings.documented: crc_sdk/connectors/blocks.py:20-30 states the convention for block statistics: a block needs a minimum fraction of valid days.
findings.observed: The EDO annual value is np.nanmin over whatever ten-day values exist in the year (crc_sdk/providers/jrc_edo.py:255), so one valid value makes a year.
findings.title: The EDO annual minimum has no completeness rule

findings.consequence: If a store changed its units, ERA5 values would be converted wrongly without an error.
findings.observed: The CMIP6 and NEX readers refuse a variable whose units attribute differs from the recipe's (crc_sdk/providers/cmip6.py:946-958). The ERA5 provider reads a units attribute only for the time axis (crc_sdk/providers/era5.py:244) and applies the kelvin and metre conversions unconditionally.

findings.documented: AGENTS.md (crc-sdk) asks contributors to 'record licence, attribution, retrieval time and checksums for every source'. docs/data-licences.md:36 lists IBTrACS as a U.S. government work with attribution requested.
findings.observed: The manifest written beside the snapshot holds url, version, subset, sha256, retrieved_at, etag, last_modified, units, terms_url and citation (crc_sdk/workflows/ibtracs.py:139-153). findings.consequence: A user cannot read NASA's latest revision through crc-sdk, and the default (1.0) is the oldest. The differences seen here are small; other models, variables and regions were not compared. NASA's technical note for version 2.0 (31 May 2025, section 4.3) states that tasmax and tasmin were reprocessed in their entirety with a corrected observational reference (an artifact over central Canada) and that values were swapped in grid cells where the maximum was below the minimum; that anomalously large pr values in cells with an extremely small daily climatology were adjusted; and that bounds were applied to hurs, huss, rlds and sfcWind. These corrections are in version 2.0 only.
findings.documented: docs/sources/cmip6.md:73: 'File revisions 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2 are selected explicitly'. crc_sdk/workflows/nex.py:84-85 refuses any other version.
evidence: NASA technical note for version 2.0, sections 3.2.2.1 and 4.3 (docs/validation/references/nex-gddp-cmip6-v2/README.md)
findings.observed: For ACCESS-CM2 r1i1p1f1, NASA's archive holds files ending in _v2.0.nc for tasmax, tasmin and pr, in both years checked (historical 2014, ssp585 2050). They were uploaded on 1 July 2025 and carry the attribute version = '2.0'. No version 1.2 file exists for these; version 1.1 exists for pr only. In the Texas box the annual one-day rainfall from 2.0 equals that from 1.1 and differs from 1.0 in 15 of 2,158 cells in 2014 (by at most 0.08 mm) and 42 cells in 2050 (by at most 0.84 mm); the annual maximum temperature from 2.0 equals that from 1.0.
findings.title: NASA serves files of version 2.0, which cannot be requested

sources.notes: Draft. Assessed on the 1.5 degree store (wb2-1p5), the Texas box (80 grid cells), the rainfall recipes for 2021, with and without the land mask. One variable-year of this store is about 0.9 GB whatever the box, because every chunk covers the globe. The temperature recipes, the 0.25 degree store and the fitted curves were not run.
sources.publisher: ECMWF / Copernicus C3S (public Zarr copies by Google and WeatherBench2)
sources.purpose: A historical baseline of annual temperature and rainfall extremes on H3 cells, comparable with the projection recipes.

statement.note: Confirmed for wb2-1p5 only. arco-0p25 was not opened: one variable-year there is about 8,800 global chunks.
statement.text: Opens one of two public Zarr copies of hourly ERA5 anonymously, with zarr over gcsfs: `arco-0p25` (the default, gs://gcp-public-data-arco-era5/ar/full_37-1h-0p25deg-chunk-1.zarr-v3, 0.25 degree) or `wb2-1p5` (gs://weatherbench2/datasets/era5/1959-2022-1h-240x121_equiangular_with_poles_conservative.zarr, 1.5 degree). No checksum of the hourly data is taken.

Names the release `final-through-<date>`. The date is the store's `valid_time_stop` attribute; for a store without it (wb2-1p5) it is 31 December of a year written in the code, 2022. Only `latest` or that name is accepted.

Accepts the years from the store's first year (1959 for wb2-1p5, written in the code) to the last complete year of that release; for rainfall the last year must be followed by one more day of record. The years are not compared with the store's time axis: hours the axis does not hold are skipped without an error.
Decodes the time axis from its `units` attribute (`hours`, `days` or `seconds since <date>`) as whole numbers; the `calendar` attribute is not read. Days are UTC days.
Reads `2m_temperature` for `txx` and `tnn` and `total_precipitation` for `rx1day` and `rx5day`, and requires the array to have exactly the dimensions time, latitude and longitude, in any order.

statement.note: The check confirms that the assumption holds for wb2-1p5 today. That the attribute is not read is shown in the offline tests on a constructed store that declares another unit (see finding CRC-006-ERA5).
statement.text: Assumes 2 m temperature in kelvin and precipitation in metres. The `units` attribute the store declares for the variable is not read.

statement.note: Confirmed for a box of 8 by 10 cells. A box narrower than one cell and a box at the 180 degree meridian were not run.
statement.text: Selects the grid cells whose centres lie inside the box grown by half a cell on every side, with longitudes brought to -180..180 and ordered west to east. A box narrower than one cell is widened to two cells. The same box is applied a second time to the stored annual file.
With `land_only`, keeps a cell only where the store's `land_sea_mask` is 0.5 or more; the others get no value.

statement.note: The chunks read from the publisher hold no NaN in the box. Missing hours inside a chunk were exercised in the offline tests only; absent chunks were exercised by the years the reference copy does not hold. The reading of an absent chunk as NaN is zarr's behaviour and has no line in crc-sdk.
statement.text: Treats a value that is not finite as missing. A chunk the store does not hold is read as the array's fill value (NaN), so it is missing too, without an error.

statement.note: Not run on the publisher's data in this draft (one variable-year is about 0.7 GB). Confirmed on constructed files only.
statement.text: Subtracts 273.15 from every hourly temperature, before any reduction, to give degrees Celsius.
Multiplies every hourly precipitation value by 1,000, before any reduction, to give millimetres.

statement.note: Not run on the publisher's data in this draft. Confirmed on constructed files only.
statement.text: The daily maximum (`txx`) or minimum (`tnn`) is taken over the hours stamped 00:00 to 23:00 UTC; a day needs at least 18 of its 24 hours.
An hourly precipitation value is counted in the UTC day of its stamp less one hour (the value stamped 00:00 belongs to the day before). A day is the sum of its 24 hours and needs all 24.

statement.note: In the year read every cell has 364 of 365 days, so the 90 per cent line itself was crossed only in the offline tests.
statement.text: Gives a grid cell an annual value only when at least 90 per cent of the year's days have a value (329 of 365, 330 of 366).

statement.note: Not run on the publisher's data in this draft. Confirmed on constructed files only.
statement.text: `txx` is the highest daily maximum of the year and `tnn` the lowest daily minimum.

`rx1day` is the largest daily total of the year. `rx5day` is the largest sum over five consecutive days that all have a value and lie within the year; windows do not reach into the neighbouring years.

statement.note: The 32-bit rounding is confirmed by the annual values. The manifest and the reuse of stored years were not exercised: every run used an empty cache folder.
statement.text: Keeps each year's values for the recipe and area as 32-bit floats in one small NetCDF file, listed with its checksum in a manifest; the annual values returned are those 32-bit values. Hourly data is never kept. The file's name does not depend on the release.

`annual_extremes()` returns one row per year and grid cell that has a value: year, latitude and longitude of the cell centre as the store writes them (longitude in -180..180), value in the recipe's unit; ordered by year, then in the store's latitude order, then west to east.

statement.note: Not checked: the fitting belongs to a later tier. A request of four years was accepted and one of fewer was not tried (finding CRC-002-FWK is about this rule).
statement.text: Refuses a request of fewer years than `minimum_years` (20 by default, never fewer than 4). Each grid cell is then fitted when it has at least 4 annual values.

statement.note: Not checked: the fitted curve (family, method, assignment to H3 cells) belongs to a later tier.
statement.text: Fits to each cell's annual values a generalised extreme value distribution by sample L-moments (the default for all four recipes), on H3 cells of resolution 5 by default, and writes the canonical hazard file.

statement.note: Not checked: these labels are written when the curve is fitted, which this draft does not run. `annual_extremes()` returns the four value columns only.
statement.text: Labels the fitted file with the store's address, the licence CC-BY-4.0, a Copernicus attribution with the retrieval year, the retrieval time, a checksum of the annual files' checksums, the window of years, `single_member` pooling and `annual_exceedance`.

sources.notes: Longitudes in NOAA's files are not wrapped to -180..180 (values up to 266.9 occur where a track crosses the date line); crc-sdk passes them through as strings. SEASON runs to 2027 because southern-hemisphere seasons are labelled by their second year. About four values in five are missing: most columns belong to one agency each.
sources.purpose: Best-track points of tropical cyclones by basin, as published, for inspection. Not asset winds or return-period curves.

statement.text: Requests `<root>/ibtracs.<subset>.list.v04r01.csv`, with the subset spelled exactly as one of the eleven names crc-sdk accepts.
Saves the response unchanged as `source.csv` and records its SHA-256. A download shorter than the announced length is refused.
Reads line 1 as column names and line 2 as units. Requires the columns SID, SEASON and ISO_TIME. The units go to the manifest only; they are not in the data.
Keeps every column, in the file's order, under NOAA's names.
Delivers every value as a string. Nothing is parsed into a number or a date, and no unit is converted.
Removes leading and trailing whitespace from every value.
Turns a value that is empty after trimming into null. NOAA marks a missing value with a single space.
Keeps every data row in the file's order. Rows are not dropped, merged, sorted or de-duplicated.
`for_storms(ids)` keeps the rows whose SID is in the list. These are track points, not complete storms across basin files.
`years(a, b)` keeps the rows whose SEASON, read as an integer, lies in a..b inclusive. SEASON is NOAA's season label, not the calendar year of the point.
Writes a manifest beside the snapshot with the address, version, subset, SHA-256, retrieval time, ETag, Last-Modified, units, a terms address and a citation. The batches themselves carry no metadata.

statement.note: Read in the code, not shown on data: showing it needs NOAA to change a file between two runs. Left to monitoring (phase V4).
statement.text: In `reuse` mode (the default) a cached snapshot is served without asking NOAA whether the file has changed. NOAA rewrites these files in place.

sources.notes: Draft. NOAA lists 126 stations with this product; ten are in Texas. A station without the product is answered with HTTP 200 and an empty body of the usual shape, which crc-sdk refuses. NOAA sends no ETag and no Last-Modified for these responses. The exceedance levels carry the datum label in capitals (MHHW) and the annual series in lower case (mhhw); crc-sdk passes both on as published. NOAA sometimes answers the same address with the values rounded to one decimal instead of two or three (seen 2026-11-12); crc-sdk delivers whichever answer it received.
sources.purpose: NOAA's published exceedance levels and annual extremes at tide stations, as published.

statement.text: Accepts a station only as a string of exactly seven digits 0-9; anything else raises ValueError before any request.

Makes three GET requests to `https://api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/dpapi/prod/webapi/product.json` with `name=extremewaterlevels`, the station and `units=metric`: one with nothing more (station), one with `details=exceedancelevels&levelType=high` (levels), one with `extremeType=annuals&levelType=high` (annuals). Low-water and monthly products are never requested.

statement.note: The check compares with a second download of the same address, so it also differs when NOAA answers the same address differently (step one-answer); it cannot tell the two apart.
statement.text: Saves each response unchanged as `source.json` and records its SHA-256 in a manifest beside it.
Asks each address once and takes that answer as the station's published values. Nothing asks a second time or compares two answers; the recorded SHA-256 is that of the one answer received.

statement.note: Read in the code, not shown on data: NOAA's responses are a few kilobytes and complete. No constructed test was written for it.
statement.text: Refuses a response longer than 4 MiB (4,194,304 bytes) or shorter than its announced Content-Length.

statement.note: On NOAA's data two of these rules fire: an empty station list (a station without the product) and a levels response without the station id (NOAA sent an error message in its place). Each of the other rules is confirmed on constructed responses only, in the tests.
statement.text: Refuses a station (ValueError, nothing cached) unless: the station response lists exactly one station with that id, a longitude in -180..180, a latitude in -90..90 and a non-empty epoch; the levels and annuals responses carry that id, `units` equal to `meters` and a non-empty datum; the two datum labels are equal when letter case is ignored; the annuals response has a non-empty notice, a trend that is null or a number, and for every extreme an integer year and a finite value; the levels response has a non-empty `GEV_HI.exceedanceLevels` in which every probability is in (0, 1] and not repeated, every return period is at least 1, every level is finite, and a confidence bound that is present lies on its side of the level. There is no rule about the length or completeness of the annual series.

`source_levels()` gives one row per entry of `GEV_HI.exceedanceLevels`, in NOAA's order, with eleven columns: the station id, then name, longitude, latitude and datum epoch from the station response repeated on every row, the datum label from the levels response, and NOAA's `probability`, `returnPeriod`, `level`, `lower90CI` and `upper90CI`. A missing confidence bound becomes null. The return period is NOAA's rounded label, not 1/probability. `GEV_LO` and the monthly groups are not delivered.

`annual_extremes()` gives one row per entry of `extremes` in the annuals response, in NOAA's order, with six columns: the station id, `year`, `value`, the datum label from the annuals response, the datum epoch from the station response and NOAA's notice repeated on every row. No year is added, dropped or filled.
Delivers numbers as 64-bit floats (the year as a 32-bit integer) with NOAA's values: nothing is rounded, no unit is converted (metres are requested and required) and no datum is transformed.

`source_info()` gives the whole station entry as NOAA sent it, the datum label and units of the levels response, and the trend, its units, its start and end dates and the notice of the annuals response. The trend (mm/yr) appears here only, not in the tables.

Writes for each response a manifest with the address, station id, resource name, SHA-256, retrieval time, ETag, Last-Modified, an attribution, a documentation address and a terms address. The tables themselves carry no metadata.
With `cache(dir, sha256={resource: digest})` a response whose SHA-256 is not the given one is refused with RuntimeError; the names accepted are station, levels and annuals.

statement.note: Read in the code and in crc-sdk's own test (tests/test_noaa_water_levels.py), not shown on data: showing it needs NOAA to fail or change between two requests.
statement.text: Keeps the three responses of one fetch together as one snapshot; `refresh` fetches all three again, moves a pointer to the new snapshot and deletes the old one, and a fetch that fails leaves the previous snapshot in place.

statement.note: Read in the code, not shown on data: showing it needs NOAA to change a response between two runs. Left to monitoring.
statement.text: In `reuse` mode (the default) a complete cached snapshot is served without asking NOAA whether the responses have changed. NOAA sends neither ETag nor Last-Modified for them.

sources.notes: Assessed on the stations the Texas data explorer uses: the first forty USW stations in the Texas box, 2000 to 2024. These are small airports whose records begin around 2005, so 592 of 1,000 station-years have a file, 8 stations reach 15 complete years and none reaches crc-sdk's default of 20. Days are UTC days: in Texas a UTC day runs from the local evening to the next. The values are extremes of sampled hourly temperature, not of an instrument's daily maximum and minimum.
sources.purpose: Annual extremes of hourly station temperature, fitted per station, as a local check on gridded curves.

statement.text: Reads one Parquet file per station and year, `<root>/<year>/parquet/GHCNh_<station>_<year>.parquet`. A file NOAA does not have (HTTP 404) gives a year with no value; other errors stop the run.
Reads eight columns by range requests tied to the file's ETag: STATION, DATE, LATITUDE, LONGITUDE, ELEVATION, temperature and its quality and source codes. Hourly files are not kept.
Reads DATE as a timestamp and keeps the reports of the requested station whose timestamp falls in the requested year. A report whose DATE cannot be read is dropped.

statement.note: In these files the excluded reports carried other quality codes. No report had code 1 or 5 from an unlisted source, so on NOAA's data the source lists were not put to the test; the offline tests exercise them on constructed files.
statement.text: Uses a temperature when its quality code is blank, or is 1 from one of fourteen listed source codes, or is 5 from one of eight listed source codes. Any other code excludes the report's value.
Uses a temperature only if it is a finite number between -93.2 and 61.8 degrees Celsius inclusive.
Takes the temperature in degrees Celsius as published. No unit is converted; the output is labelled degC.

Groups reports by UTC calendar day. For each day it counts all reports, the accepted reports and the distinct clock hours that hold an accepted report, and takes the lowest and highest accepted temperature.
Counts a day as valid when at least 18 distinct hours hold an accepted report (three quarters of 24, rounded up). Several reports in one hour count once.
Counts a year as complete when at least 90 per cent of its days are valid (329 of 365, 330 of 366).

For a complete year, takes the highest daily maximum (`temperature_max`) or the lowest daily minimum (`temperature_min`) over the valid days only. An incomplete year has no value. Values on days that are not valid are ignored.

statement.note: No station in these files moved or lacked coordinates, so the refusal was not seen on NOAA's data; the offline tests exercise it on constructed files.
statement.text: Places the station at the lowest latitude and lowest longitude reported in the year, with the lowest reported elevation (-999.9 read as missing). Refuses a station whose coordinates move by more than 0.05 degrees within a year.
Fits a curve for a station only when it has at least the policy's minimum of complete years (20 by default; 15 in the Texas data explorer). The minimum is applied per station.

statement.note: Confirmed here: the family named in the output. The fit itself (parameters, method, behaviour on short records) is not checked; it belongs to validation (phase V7).
statement.text: Fits a generalized extreme value distribution to annual maxima and a lower-tail Gumbel distribution to annual minima, both by L-moments.
Writes the licence (CC0-1.0), an attribution text, the latest retrieval time, a checksum over the cached daily files and the request into the curve file's metadata.

statement.text: Reads one NetCDF file per variable, model, scenario, member and year from NASA's archive on AWS, by range requests. Nothing is cached and no checksum is taken.
Reads exactly the file version asked for (1.0 has no suffix in the file name; later ones end in `_v<version>`). A version NASA does not have fails; another is never substituted.
Accepts the file versions 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2.
Checks that the file's own attributes name the model, scenario, member and version that were asked for.

statement.note: The warning was seen on every file read. `strict_licence=True` was not run.
statement.text: Reads the model licence written in the file and keeps it beside NASA's archive licence (CC0-1.0). Warns when the file's licence is not CC0; refuses it when `strict_licence` is set.
Requires precipitation to be declared in kg m-2 s-1 and multiplies it by 86,400 to give millimetres per day.
Requires temperature to be declared in kelvin (K) and subtracts 273.15 to give degrees Celsius.

statement.note: The files read use the proleptic Gregorian calendar with 365 days and no gap. Other calendars and gaps were exercised only in the offline tests.
statement.text: Requires the daily time axis to be strictly increasing and to lie within the requested year, in the file's own calendar, and places each day by its date.

statement.note: Confirmed for a box of 44 by 53 cells. A box narrower than one cell and a box across the 180 degree meridian were not run.
statement.text: Selects the grid cells whose centres lie inside the box grown by half a cell on every side, with longitudes brought to -180..180 and ordered west to east. A box narrower than one cell is widened to two cells.
Treats the file's fill value as missing.

statement.note: In NASA's files a cell has either every day or none (ocean), so the 90 per cent line itself was crossed only in the offline tests.
statement.text: Gives a grid cell a value only when at least 90 per cent of the year's days are present.
`rx1day` is the largest daily value of the year. `rx5day` is the largest sum over five consecutive days that lie within the year; windows do not reach into the neighbouring years.

statement.note: Cannot be checked at crc-sdk 0.11.1, where both recipes fail (CRC-001-NEX). On a local clone that carries the fix, every cell agrees with the recomputation (checks `annual-fixed-clone`); that is not a statement about a released version.
statement.text: `txx` is the highest daily maximum of the year and `tnn` the lowest daily minimum.
Returns one row per grid cell that has a value, at the cell's centre, south to north and west to east. No distribution is fitted.

Labels every row with the unit, recipe, model, scenario, member, grid, version, calendar (under one name per calendar: `365_day` is written `noleap`), the file's address, the retrieval time, both licences and an attribution.
